findings.reason: citing the existing stranded-launch owner changes §16's mechanism and its test (write-time prevention vs. extending the release) and may collapse the section.
findings.text: §16 proposes a new pre-admission launch guarantee for the plan-review pointer without citing `_stranded_launch` (`reckon/crew/recovery.py:6602`) and `_discard_stranded_review` (`reckon/crew/recovery.py:1331`), which already detect and release a pidless pre-spawn pointer past the bound — the exact state §16 measures — so the section may be adding a second owner of one lifecycle instead of extending the first

findings.reason: the author must name the reader/owner of the member session lock before implementation, or the node re-derives it.
findings.text: §11 adds dispatch-side detection of a busy member and hold-or-divert without naming the mechanism that exposes the member's writer-lock (`thread-store ... already has an active writer`), so the plan proposes a subsystem with no citation of the machinery it must read

findings.reason: reframing §16 to extend dispatch's one pointer-write ordering (as §5 already does for refusals) changes the section's target file and its done-when.
findings.text: the plan-review launch is a thin layer over dispatch's launch (`recovery._dispatch_composed_review` calls `reckon.crew.dispatch`), and §16 special-cases the plan-review path for a pointer-write ordering that lives in dispatch's shared path, without saying why that ordering cannot simply be fixed once for every lane

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §17 records that the per-run supervisor has no module boundary and schedules one whose interface is the spec it reads and the run-directory records it writes; the landed body (`_run_supervisor`, `_supervisor_spec`, `_supervisor_argv`, `_start_supervisor`, `_spawn_detached_supervisor`, `_spawn_through_fleet`, `_confirm_supervisor_survived`, `_write_boundary_tree_snapshot`, `supervisor_main.py`) is exactly the spread §17 exists to fold.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — §18 names the owner to extend (`fleet_supervisor.state_directory`, `reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py:253`) for the fleet-record path that `dispatch._fleet_record_path` (`reckon/crew/dispatch.py:9648`) re-derives, and `fleet_node.py:306` already reads it through that owner.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §11 (busy-member hold/divert) and §16 (the stranded plan-review pointer) each add machinery without citing the mechanism each most resembles: §16's "pre-spawn pointer that never spawned" state is already owned by `_stranded_launch`/`_discard_stranded_review` in `reckon/crew/recovery.py`, and §11 names no reader of the member's session writer-lock.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §16 treats the pre-admission pointer write as a plan-review defect, but `recovery._dispatch_composed_review` reaches the same `dispatch` path every launch takes, so the pointer is written by dispatch's shared write-ordering; the section does not say why dispatch's ordering cannot be extended instead of a plan-review-specific guarantee.
